content:
## Sub-query: What are the actual VRAM requirements of current open-source models in 2025-2026?

---

## Key Findings

### 1. LLM VRAM Requirements (Full Precision & Quantized)

The universal formula: **VRAM ≈ (Parameters × Bytes-per-Weight) + KV Cache + ~10-20% Overhead**. At Q4_K_M (the industry-standard "sweet spot"), this works out to roughly **0.5–0.6 GB per billion parameters** for weights alone.

#### Comprehensive LLM VRAM Table (Q4_K_M Quantization)

| Model | Total Params | VRAM (Q4_K_M weights) | Recommended Total VRAM | Fits Single Consumer GPU? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Phi-4 Mini** | 3.8B | ~2.5 GB | 4–6 GB | ✅ Any GPU |
| **Qwen3-4B** | 4B | ~2.5 GB | 4–6 GB | ✅ Any GPU |
| **Gemma 3 4B** | 4B | ~2.2 GB | 4–6 GB | ✅ Any GPU |
| **Llama 3.1 8B** | 8B | ~5 GB | 8–10 GB | ✅ 8GB+ |
| **Qwen3-8B** | 8B | ~5 GB | 8–10 GB | ✅ 8GB+ |
| **DeepSeek-R1 8B Distill** | 8B | ~5 GB | 6–8 GB | ✅ 8GB+ |
| **Mistral 7B** | 7B | ~4.5 GB | 6–8 GB | ✅ 8GB+ |
| **Gemma 3 12B** | 12B | ~6.7 GB | 10–12 GB | ✅ 12GB+ |
| **Mistral Nemo 12B** | 12B | ~8 GB | 10–12 GB | ✅ 12GB+ |
| **Phi-4 14B** | 14B | ~9 GB | 12–14 GB | ✅ 16GB+ |
| **Qwen3-14B** | 14B | ~9 GB | 12–16 GB | ✅ 16GB+ |
| **Qwen3-32B** | 32B | ~19.5 GB | 24–32 GB | ✅ 24GB (tight) |
| **DeepSeek-R1 32B Distill** | 32B | ~18 GB | 18–24 GB | ✅ 24GB |
| **Gemma 3 27B** | 27B | ~15 GB | 17–22 GB | ✅ 24GB |
| **Mixtral 8x7B (MoE)** | 47B total | ~24 GB | 24–28 GB | ⚠️ Tight on 24GB |
| **Llama 3.3 70B** | 70B | ~40 GB | 42–50 GB | ❌ Need 2×24GB or 48GB |
| **DeepSeek-R1 70B Distill** | 70B | ~40 GB | 40–48 GB | ❌ Need multi-GPU |
| **Llama 4 Scout (MoE)** | 109B total (17B active) | ~34 GB (IQ1_S) / ~66 GB (Q4) | 36–70 GB | ❌ Multi-GPU needed for Q4 |
| **Qwen3-235B-A22B (MoE)** | 235B total (22B active) | ~117 GB (Q4) | 130+ GB | ❌ Requires massive multi-GPU |
| **Llama 4 Maverick (MoE)** | 400B total | ~122 GB (1.78-bit) / ~200 GB (Q4) | 130–220+ GB | ❌ Datacenter-class |
| **DeepSeek-R1 Full** | 671B | ~350 GB+ | 360+ GB | ❌ Datacenter only |

**Critical MoE Note:** Mixture-of-Experts models (Llama 4, Qwen3-235B, etc.) must load ALL expert weights into memory even though only a fraction (~17-22B) are active per token. VRAM is determined by **total** parameters, not active parameters.

---

### 2. Image Generation Model VRAM Requirements

| Model | Precision | VRAM Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Stable Diffusion 1.5** | FP16 | ~4 GB (min), 8 GB rec. | Lightweight, mature |
| **SDXL** | FP16 | ~6-8 GB (min), 12-16 GB rec. | Standard for quality work |
| **SD 3.5 Medium** | FP16 | ~10 GB | Good balance |
| **SD 3.5 Large** | FP16 | ~18 GB | 8B param model |
| **Flux.1 Dev/Schnell** | FP16 | 18–24 GB | DiT architecture, very demanding |
| **Flux.1 Dev/Schnell** | FP8 | 13–15 GB | Good compromise |
| **Flux.1 Dev/Schnell** | NF4/GGUF Q4 | 6–10 GB | Accessible to mid-range GPUs |

**Key insight:** For modern image gen with ControlNet + LoRAs + higher resolutions, **12-16 GB is the practical floor**, and **24 GB** is strongly recommended for full-precision Flux workflows.

---

### 3. Voice/Audio Model VRAM Requirements

#### Speech-to-Text (Whisper ASR)
| Model Size | Parameters | VRAM |
|---|---|---|
| Tiny | 39M | ~1 GB |
| Base | 74M | ~1 GB |
| Small | 244M | ~2 GB |
| Medium | 769M | ~5 GB |
| Turbo | 809M | ~6 GB |
| Large-v3 | 1.55B | ~10 GB |

**Tip:** `faster-whisper` achieves 3-4x speedup over standard implementation.

#### Text-to-Speech (TTS)
| Model | VRAM | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Kokoro-82M | <2-3 GB | Fast, runs on CPU or low-VRAM GPUs |
| Chatterbox Turbo | ~2-4 GB | Low-latency, optimized for voice agents |
| Zonos-v0.1 | ~6 GB+ | Emotional control, voice cloning |
| VoxCPM2 | ~6 GB+ | 48kHz output, voice cloning |
| XTTS v2 | ~8 GB+ | Popular but outperformed by newer models |

**Summary:** Voice/audio is the **least VRAM-demanding** category. 8 GB handles most use cases comfortably. Only advanced voice cloning or running full STT+TTS pipelines simultaneously alongside an LLM pushes toward 12-16 GB.

---

### 4. Video Generation Model VRAM Requirements

| Model | Variant | VRAM (Optimized) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Wan 2.1/2.2** | 1.3B | 4–8 GB | Budget-friendly, ~4 min for 5s 480p clip |
| **Wan 2.1/2.2** | 14B (480p) | 18–22 GB (FP8) | RTX 4090 can handle this |
| **Wan 2.1/2.2** | 14B (720p) | 22–26 GB (FP8) | At 24GB card limit, often fails |
| **Wan 2.1/2.2** | 14B (720p+ full) | 54–65 GB | Multi-GPU/cloud required |
| **CogVideoX** | 2B | ~8 GB | Fast iteration, lower VRAM |
| **CogVideoX** | 5B | 12–16 GB | Requires FP8/tiling |

**Critical reality:** Video generation is the most VRAM-hungry category. Even with optimization, the 14B Wan model at 720p pushes beyond 24 GB. Generation times are long: ~12+ minutes per clip on RTX 4090. This is a frontier use case where 24 GB is barely adequate and 32+ GB is ideal.

---

### 5. Real-World Performance Benchmarks (Tokens/Second)

#### Usability Tiers
| Speed | User Experience |
|---|---|
| **<10 t/s** | Barely interactive; trigger-and-wait |
| **10-20 t/s** | Minimum functional for chat (matches reading speed) |
| **30-40 t/s** | Comfortable "sweet spot" for interactive use |
| **60-100+ t/s** | High-performance; agentic workflows, rapid coding |

#### Performance by VRAM/GPU Tier (Q4_K_M models)

| VRAM Tier | Model Size Range | Typical Speed | Example GPU |
|---|---|---|---|
| **8 GB** | 7-9B only | 30-60 t/s | RTX 4060 |
| **12 GB** | 7-14B | 20-40 t/s | RTX 3060 12GB |
| **16 GB** | 14-20B | 20-40 t/s | RTX 4070 Ti Super |
| **24 GB** | 30-35B comfortably | 30-45 t/s (8B), 30-40 t/s (32B) | RTX 4090 |
| **32 GB** | 32-46B comfortably | 60-100+ t/s (8B), varies larger | RTX 5090 |

#### Specific GPU Benchmarks (2025-2026)
| GPU | Model | Speed |
|---|---|---|
| RTX 4090 (24GB) | Llama 3.1 8B | ~165 t/s |
| RTX 5090 (32GB) | Llama 3.1 8B | ~213 t/s (+29%) |
| RTX 4090 | Qwen3 14B | ~98 t/s |
| RTX 5090 | Qwen3 14B | ~148 t/s (+51%) |
| RTX 4090 | Qwen3 32B (Q4) | ~45 t/s |
| RTX 5090 | Qwen3 32B (Q4) | ~61 t/s (+36%) |

**The "bandwidth cliff":** If a model doesn't fit entirely in VRAM and spills to system RAM, performance crashes from 30-100+ t/s down to **1-5 t/s**. This is the single most important factor — partial offloading is a massive penalty.

**The formula:** `Tokens/sec ≈ Memory Bandwidth (GB/s) ÷ Model Size (GB)` (real-world is ~50-80% of theoretical).

---

### 6. Local Inference Tools & Their VRAM Requirements

| Tool | Backend | Best For | VRAM Strategy |
|---|---|---|---|
| **LM Studio** | llama.cpp / MLX | Beginners, GUI, A/B testing | Auto-manages; visual VRAM monitoring |
| **Ollama** | llama.cpp | Developers, API integration | "Docker for LLMs"; auto-allocates |
| **llama.cpp** | Native | Max control, low-VRAM, CPU | Granular layer offloading (-ngl); allows GPU/CPU split |
| **vLLM** | Native | Production serving, multi-user | PagedAttention; crashes on OOM (no spill to RAM) |
| **ComfyUI** | PyTorch | Image/video generation | Dynamic offloading; best for Flux/SD/Wan |

**Key insight:** Ollama and LM Studio are thin wrappers around llama.cpp — performance is nearly identical when configured the same way. The tool choice doesn't significantly affect VRAM requirements for single-user use; hardware is the bottleneck.

**Embedding models for RAG:** Extremely lightweight. nomic-embed-text needs ~0.3-0.5 GB; all-MiniLM needs ~0.1-0.3 GB. These are negligible alongside any LLM.

---

## Evidence Table

| Source | Key Claim | Tier |
|---|---|---|
| willitrunai.com | Llama 3.3 70B Q4_K_M needs ~40-44 GB for weights | Tier B (verified tool) |
| unsloth.ai | Llama 4 Scout 109B at IQ1_S needs ~34 GB VRAM | Tier A (model publisher) |
| stability.ai | SD 3.5 Medium requires ~9.9 GB FP16 | Tier A (official) |
| localllm.in | 8 GB VRAM fits 7-9B models; 24 GB fits 30-35B at Q4 | Tier B (community reference) |
| HuggingFace GGUF Calculator | Community tool for calculating VRAM from model architecture | Tier A (verified tool) |
| Reddit/community consensus | 10-20 t/s is minimum usable; <10 t/s feels sluggish | Tier B (verified by multiple sources) |
| Multiple benchmarks | RTX 4090: ~165 t/s on 8B; ~45 t/s on 32B Q4 | Tier B (aggregated benchmarks) |
| Multiple benchmarks | RTX 5090: 29-51% faster than 4090 due to bandwidth | Tier B (multiple sources agree) |
| Community consensus | CPU offloading drops speed to 1-5 t/s | Tier B (widely confirmed) |

---

## Counter-Evidence Considered

1. **"Small models are good enough":** SLMs (1B-4B) are genuinely impressive in 2025-2026 for targeted tasks (summarization, classification, simple coding). A 3-4B model on 4-8 GB VRAM is usable. **However**, these models are not competitive with 14B-32B models for complex reasoning, multi-step coding, or agentic workflows. The counter-argument has merit for casual users but not for power users wanting frontier local AI.

2. **"Apple Silicon solves the VRAM problem":** Unified Memory (up to 128 GB on M4 Max) allows running 70B+ models locally. **However**, Apple Silicon has lower memory bandwidth than discrete GPUs (~546 GB/s M4 Max vs. ~1,792 GB/s RTX 5090), so tokens/sec is slower per unit of compute. It's a valid alternative path but doesn't eliminate the need for large memory — it just provides it differently.

3. **"Quantization makes VRAM irrelevant":** Aggressive quantization (1-2 bit) can dramatically shrink models. **However**, below Q4 (4-bit), model quality degrades noticeably. There's a floor below which you lose too much capability. Q4_K_M remains the community standard because lower is visibly worse.

4. **"CPU offloading makes any model runnable on any hardware":** Technically true, but practically false for interactive use. Offloading to RAM drops speeds to 1-5 t/s, which is barely tolerable for any interactive use.

---

## Gaps

1. **Exact laptop GPU benchmarks:** Most benchmarks focus on desktop GPUs (RTX 4090/5090). Laptop GPU benchmarks (RTX 4060/4070 Laptop, which have lower power/bandwidth) are less documented but would show ~30-50% lower performance than desktop equivalents.

2. **Combined workload VRAM:** Running an LLM + embedding model + image generation simultaneously is a real use case but poorly benchmarked. In practice, you'd need to swap models in/out of VRAM or have enough to hold multiple models.

3. **Fine-tuning VRAM requirements:** Local fine-tuning/LoRA training was out of scope but typically requires 2-3x the inference VRAM due to optimizer states and gradients. This is almost impractical below 24 GB for useful model sizes.

4. **Specific 2026 laptop GPU lineups:** The exact laptop GPU options available in September 2026 (RTX 50-series laptop variants, potential 16GB/24GB laptop GPUs) would affect the recommendation but depend on hardware research.

---

## Summary Recommendation Matrix

| VRAM | What You Can Run Comfortably | Limitation |
|---|---|---|
| **8 GB** | 7-8B LLMs, SD 1.5/SDXL, Whisper Small, basic TTS | Can't run 14B+ models; limited context; no Flux/SD3 at full quality |
| **12 GB** | 12-14B LLMs, SDXL, Flux Q4, Whisper Large, Wan 1.3B video | 27B+ models need offloading (slow); limited Flux quality |
| **16 GB** | 14-20B LLMs, Flux FP8, good context windows | 27B+ tight; no 32B without offloading |
| **24 GB** | 27-35B LLMs, Flux FP16, Wan 14B 480p, all voice models | 70B+ impossible on single card; video gen limited at 720p+ |
| **32 GB** | 32-46B LLMs comfortably, all image gen, video gen at higher quality | 70B still needs quantization; MoE models (100B+) still too large |
